data.name: Sriya
data.gender_notes: Sriya is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Sriya is the name of the goddess Lakshmi, who represents wealth, prosperity, and good fortune. She is the consort of Vishnu and is often depicted with gold coins in her hands. The name Sriya carries the meaning “Goddess of Wealth and Prosperity” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Tamil, Telugu. Parents who choose Sriya usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of wealth and prosperity and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Sriya is a symbol of abundance, prosperity, and spiritual wealth. It represents the inner riches of the soul and the outer abundance of material possessions.
data.etymology: Sriya belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Goddess of Wealth and Prosperity.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Sriya total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

data.cultural_impact: Sriya is a popular name in the Hindu culture, particularly in the Southern states of India. It is considered an auspicious name and is often given to baby girls in the belief that it will bless them with good fortune, wealth, and prosperity. The name is also commonly used as a prefix for other names or as a part of compound names, such as Sriya Lakshmi or Sriya Devi.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hinduism, Sriya is the name of the goddess Lakshmi, who is the embodiment of wealth, prosperity, and good fortune. Her name is derived from the Sanskrit words "shri" meaning "auspicious" and "yaa" meaning "she who brings." The name signifies the presence of Lakshmi's blessings and is believed to bring prosperity, abundance, and happiness to those who bear it. The name is also considered sacred and is often used in mantras and prayers to invoke the goddess' blessings.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Sriya, meaning 'Goddess Lakshmi's Abode', symbolizes the dwelling of prosperity and abundance in one's life. It embodies the spiritual pursuit of wealth and fortune, rooted in the belief that material wealth is a manifestation of inner peace and happiness.

historical_references.reference: Sriya was an ancient Indian princess, the daughter of King Dasaratha of Ayodhya and Queen Kausalya. She is best known as the wife of Lord Rama and the mother of their sons Luv and Kush.

Sriya or Sita is a major goddess in the Hindu pantheon, revered as the embodiment of purity, devotion, and marital fidelity. She is the consort of Lord Vishnu in his avatar as Rama and is also identified with the goddess Lakshmi.
